reason: E1 supports the premise that cold rolling leaves residual dislocations causing work hardening, but no cited evidence supports the existence or role of non-uniform thermal expansion stresses in a single-phase alloy, nor their interaction with dislocations to govern thermoelastic behavior.
premises: Cold rolling introduces residual dislocation networks that cause work hardening in HfNbTaTiZr.
Non-uniform thermal expansion in a single-phase BCC matrix generates local thermal stresses.
Residual dislocations and thermal stresses interact to modify dislocation activation and recovery.
This interaction explains work hardening at intermediate temperatures and softening during high-temperature creep.
Annealing removes residual dislocations and homogenizes thermal strain fields, altering mechanical behavior.
